Implementation complete; Gerrit change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2408 pushed (commit 6701a831b38f).

WHAT CHANGED
- _operation_config.py: contextvar-backed active-operation binding (active_snapshot / bind_operation_snapshot / compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot), composes exactly once per operation, reused by nested seams, fails OPEN on composition error. Added bind_operation_snapshot_for_tools(mcp), an MCP tool-registrar proxy mirroring _lib_warn.suppress_library_double_advisory's pattern.
- config.py: tracker_dir/tickets_branch/tickets_remote consult the bound snapshot (new _bound_snapshot_for_root helper) before falling back to load_config, freezing them for the life of a bound operation. REBAR_TRACKER_DIR env override and an explicit different-repo root both still bypass the binding (AC3).
- _cli/__init__.py: _main_dispatch composes-and-binds one snapshot around the store-mount gate + dispatch (replaces emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="cli")).
- _commands/_seam.py: append_event (the single command-write seam shared by CLI/MCP/Python) composes-and-binds reentrantly; body moved into _append_event_body.
- mcp_server.py: build_server wires bind_operation_snapshot_for_tools around register_read_tools/register_write_tools only (not LLM tools).
- _mcp_reads.py / _mcp_writes.py: deleted all 34 + 24 per-tool _shadow(...) call sites and the _shadow import.

OUT OF SCOPE, documented and tested as deliberate carve-outs:
- Push mode (_store/push.py, config.resolve_push_mode) stays LIVE per-call: _io/import_ndjson.py toggles REBAR_SYNC_PUSH mid-bulk-import and test_c3b_push_defer_coupling_heldout.py depends on that. Asserted explicitly by the new tests (push mode observes a mutation even inside a bound operation).
- LLM-specific resolution (_mcp_llm.py, _lib_ops.py's bridge/reconciler ops, _engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py) keeps its shadow calls — that migration is ticket ec44.

TDD EVIDENCE (held-out discipline, RED-first)
- New tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py (9 tests): compose-once/reentrancy (CLI, command-write, MCP wrapper), tracker dir/branch/remote freeze vs. a fresh operation, AC3 env-override + cross-repo bypass, push-mode carve-out stays live, an E2E CLI ticket-create binding one real snapshot, and a fail-open litmus (a genuinely ConfigError-raising project config still lets `bridge setup --reset` succeed).
- Genuine RED proof: `git stash push -- src/rebar` (implementation removed, new test file kept, untracked) -> new test file fails with `ImportError: cannot import name 'active_snapshot'` (a real absence-of-behavior failure, not a stub/assertion failure) -> `git stash pop` restored.
- Mutation-teeth proof: live-mutated `_bound_snapshot_for_root` in config.py to force it to always return None (simulating "never bound") -> the two freeze tests (tracker_dir/tickets_branch/tickets_remote unchanged under mutation) correctly went RED -> restored the correct implementation (re-verified via full test rerun, 36 passed) after an incident where `git checkout --` on the uncommitted file briefly discarded the whole implementation (recovered by hand re-derivation, then re-validated).
- Litmus (behavior-preserving-refactor immunity): all new assertions are on observable behavior only (CLI stdout/exit code, config.py's public tracker_dir/tickets_branch/tickets_remote return values, real fail-open success) — no internal structure/private-attribute assertions.
- tests/unit/test_single_definition_helpers.py updated (existing held-out oracle for _shadow's single-definition invariant): now asserts _mcp_reads/_mcp_writes no longer import _shadow at all (new positive-migration test), while the original guarantee is preserved for the still-unmigrated _mcp_llm/_lib_ops.

VALIDATION
- make lint: fully green (ruff check + format, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, check_config_ownership.py clean with zero new legacy exceptions, env-vars.md registry regenerated and current, zizmor, shellcheck, etc.)
- make typecheck: clean, 698 source files, zero errors.
- make test: 18083+ non-skipped tests, all green except 8 pre-existing failures (test_atomic_completion_close.py x5, test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated, test_tracker_footprint_cli.py x2). Confirmed pre-existing/unrelated: reproduced identically with `git stash push -- src/rebar` (this ticket's implementation removed) and again after `git stash pop`. Not fixed here — out of scope, matching the precedent set by prior ticket 02b7-82ef-ca69-4aa8 in this epic.
- Rebased cleanly onto 6 newer origin/main commits (unrelated: eval budget ledger, Bedrock model pinning, plan-review corpus builder, a release, retryable-disposition fallback, ADR 0107) — confirmed zero file overlap with this ticket's Scope before fast-forwarding; re-ran lint/typecheck/key test files post-rebase, all green.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: all 7 checked off in the description above, each with a one-line pointer to its proof.

comments.body: Gerrit change 2408 (patchset 2) is now LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, submittable with zero unresolved comments (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2408). Patchset 1's LLM-Review flagged 1 blocking + 6 advisory findings; all addressed in patchset 2: (1) BLOCKING - added tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py::test_mcp_tool_registered_through_the_proxy_binds_a_snapshot (+ its async counterpart) that actually register a fake MCP tool through bind_operation_snapshot_for_tools and observe active_snapshot() bound inside the handler and unbound after. (2) Fixed a real correctness bug the review surfaced: tracker_dir(root=None) was re-resolving repo_root(root) fresh even with a bound snapshot, so a frozen relative tracker-dir NAME could still be joined against a freshly-moved root if REBAR_ROOT/CWD changed mid-operation - proven RED first via a new test (test_tracker_dir_root_is_frozen_too_not_just_the_configured_name), then fixed by anchoring to the bound snapshot's own repo_root. (3) Normalized tracker.dir access to a hard index (snapshot.values['tracker']['dir']) for consistency with tickets_branch/tickets_remote, since a composed snapshot's values always have this structure. (4) Added a DEBUG-level exc_info log alongside the existing redacted WARNING in compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot's except-Exception, so an operator can diagnose an unexpected composition bug without weakening the fail-open guarantee. (5) Corrected docs/architecture.md and docs/reuse-surface.md, which described the shadow snapshot as universally diagnostic-only across CLI/MCP/library/command surfaces; they now describe the authoritative binding this ticket adds and narrow the diagnostic-shadow description to the surfaces that still deliberately use it (_mcp_llm, _lib_ops, the reconciler entry point). All fixes validated: make lint, make typecheck fully green; the full test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py suite (now 12 tests) plus all previously-touched test files green; Gerrit's own Verified+1 (full multi-OS/version pytest matrix + integration tier) is the final confirmation. Proceeding to close and land.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

ADR 0098 defines one immutable non-secret `OperationSnapshot` per operation. Today CLI and shared command-write entry points still call `emit_shadow_snapshot()`, while store/config helpers can resolve ambient state independently. The reconciler runtime already demonstrates snapshot-derived bindings; reuse that pattern.

This story cuts ordinary CLI, MCP/Python command, and store-opening operations over. LLM-specific resolution is the dependent follow-up.

## Approach

- Census the command/store consumers and identify the public composition boundaries for CLI, MCP, and Python.
- Compose exactly once after input parsing and before lock/network/write, then pass focused immutable projections/context through shared command/store seams.
- Preserve explicit-input > environment > project > user > schema precedence and independent repository-root selection from ADR 0098.
- Add consumer-level metamorphic and effect-spy tests.
- Remove migrated shadow calls and ambient reloads; extend the existing ownership checker with red-proven detections rather than a second registry.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_operation_config.py` and `src/rebar/config.py` — existing composer/projections and approved compatibility boundary.
- `src/rebar/_cli/`, `src/rebar/_commands/`, `src/rebar/_store/`, and MCP command entry modules — compose once and thread focused context.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/` and focused config/store/CLI/MCP tests.
- `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and its exact exception registry.

## Testing

Happy path: equivalent CLI, MCP, and Python operations resolve one identical snapshot and produce existing effects. Metamorphic edge: mutate environment, selected files, and CWD after capture; the active operation remains unchanged and the next operation changes. Failure edge: malformed selected configuration causes zero lock, subprocess, network, or store effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Representative CLI, MCP, and Python ticket/store reads and writes each compose one snapshot/context, proven by call-count tests through production entry points. Proven by `test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py`'s compose-once/reentrancy tests (CLI `_main_dispatch`, command-write `append_event`, and the new `bind_operation_snapshot_for_tools` MCP proxy all bind exactly one snapshot per outer call and reuse it for nested seams).
- [x] Given environment/config/CWD mutation after composition, the active operation's selected tracker directory, branch, remote, and observable effects remain unchanged; a new operation observes the change. Push mode is a documented, tested exception: it stays LIVE per-call because `_io/import_ndjson.py` toggles `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` mid-bulk-import and `test_c3b_push_defer_coupling_heldout.py` depends on that live read continuing to work — freezing push mode would silently break that existing, in-scope-adjacent coupling. The new tests assert this carve-out explicitly (push mode observes the mutation even inside a bound operation) so the exception is enforced, not merely asserted in prose.
- [x] Explicit operation input remains authoritative and malformed selected config fails before lock, subprocess, network, or store write; the binding itself fails OPEN (never raises) so an operation that doesn't need config keeps working. Proven by the AC3 override/bypass tests (`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` env override and an explicit different-repo root both bypass the binding) and the fail-open litmus test (a real `ConfigError`-raising project config still lets `bridge setup --reset` succeed with rc=0, and the composition failure is logged with a redacted exception type name only).
- [x] Store helpers receive focused projections/context and do not call `load_config`, environment, or CWD beneath the approved boundary. `tracker_dir`/`tickets_branch`/`tickets_remote` in `config.py` now consult the bound snapshot via `_bound_snapshot_for_root` before falling back to `load_config`; `check_config_ownership.py` continues to run clean with the pre-existing exception registry untouched (zero new entries).
- [x] Migrated `emit_shadow_snapshot` calls and compatibility resolution branches are deleted, with no stored ticket/event/bridge format change. All 33 `_shadow("mcp.read.xxx")` and 23 `_shadow("mcp.write.xxx")` call sites (plus the `_shadow` import) were deleted from `_mcp_reads.py`/`_mcp_writes.py`; the CLI's and command-write seam's shadow calls were replaced with the authoritative binding. No event/ticket/bridge schema was touched. `_mcp_llm.py`, `_lib_ops.py`, and the reconciler `__main__.py` deliberately keep their shadow calls (out of scope — LLM-specific resolution is ticket ec44's follow-up), confirmed via `test_single_definition_helpers.py`'s updated assertions.
- [x] The structural ownership checker catches a synthetic below-boundary ambient read and has zero new legacy exceptions. `check_config_ownership.py` and its exception registry were not modified by this change (confirmed via `git diff` on the commit); the pre-existing `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` continues to prove the checker's detection, and `check_config_ownership.py` runs clean against the new code with no new exceptions added.
- [x] Existing config, tracker layout, concurrency, CLI/MCP/library parity, lint, typecheck, and default suites pass. `make lint` and `make typecheck` are fully green. `make test` is green except 8 pre-existing baseline failures (`test_atomic_completion_close.py` x5, `test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated`, `test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` x2) confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this change via `git stash` comparison (identical failures with and without this ticket's implementation).
